BiblicalUsage: Kecuwth means a covering, clothing, a veil: Genesis 20:16 has Abimelech giving Sarah a thousand pieces of silver, saying, he is to thee a covering of the eyes. Exodus 22:27 says the poor man's covering is his raiment for his skin, wherein shall he sleep? Deuteronomy 22:12 says thou shalt make thee fringes upon the four quarters of thy vesture, wherewith thou coverest thyself. Job 24:7 says the oppressors cause the naked to lodge without clothing, that they have no covering in the cold.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a covering is a mercy: it hides shame, it keeps a man warm, and God hears the cry of the one who has none. I hold that the law's fringes and the poor man's cloak both say the same thing, that God covers his people.
